title: Certificates of Deposit: The Instruction That Replaces an Unworkable Payout Instruction, and Which Maturity It Governs
content:
When a maturity instruction on a certificate from the Certificates of Deposit range sends the balance to a checking or savings account that is now closed, that instruction is unworkable at the end of grace. This page states what takes its place, for which certificates and for how long the replacement is owed, and which maturity it governs.

## What takes its place

- On a tier offering automatic renewal, the unworkable instruction gives way to the instruction to renew automatically.
- On a tier without automatic renewal, it gives way to the instruction to mail a check, so that the full balance leaves as an official check.

Every other maturity instruction stays exactly as it is and nothing is recorded: an instruction to renew automatically, an instruction to mail a check, and an instruction paying out into an account that is still open.

## While the replacement is owed

The replacement is owed for a certificate in active status or in its grace period, and it remains owed for as long as the grace period's outcome is unbooked, no matter how many days have gone by since the grace period itself ended. A certificate whose grace outcome has already been booked has left its grace period, and the replacement no longer concerns it.

## Which maturity a changed instruction governs

A change the owner makes to the maturity instruction governs the current maturity if it is recorded while grace is still running, and governs the next maturity if it is recorded after grace has ended. The bank-owed replacement described here is the one exception: recorded while the grace outcome is still unbooked, it governs the maturity that has just passed, since that maturity's outcome has not been booked yet.

## Truth table (hypothetical certificates)

| Instruction on record | Payout account | Certificate status | Automatic renewal available on the tier | Instruction after this rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pay out to savings | Closed | Grace period | Yes | Renew automatically |
| Pay out to checking | Closed | Active | Yes | Renew automatically |
| Pay out to savings | Closed | Grace period | No | Mail a check |
| Pay out to savings | Active | Grace period | Yes | Unchanged, nothing recorded |
| Renew automatically | (any) | Grace period | Yes | Unchanged, nothing recorded |
| Pay out to checking | Closed | Closed | Yes | Unchanged; the certificate is neither active nor in grace |

## Worked timing example (hypothetical)

A certificate matured on 1 March and its grace period ran through 11 March. On 14 March its grace outcome has still not been booked and its instruction pays out to a savings account that is closed. The certificate still stands in its grace period, so the replacement is owed, and once recorded it governs the 1 March maturity.
